# Phase26 — Complete source and requirement traceability

All 5,815 headed sections and 591 source files have an explicit disposition. Repeated mappings are retained because one source section can qualify several outcomes. Source-file and normalized section hashes bind the reviewed capture. Research, rejected alternatives, inherited owner rules and stage history are explicitly distinguished from normative product clauses. All actual implementation and release proof remains outstanding.

This register is the complete human-readable projection of the machine trace: every original part mapping, supplemental heading and file-only evidence disposition is included, along with source locators, hashes, reasons and targets. Source paths identify provenance rather than missing normative reading; the complete binding contracts are in the published specification volumes. Source files need not be fetched to reconstruct a requirement.

## Supplemental authority and correction review

# Phase26 — independent whole-source coverage review

15 September 2026. **Pass with the explicit supplemental trace map included in the publication package.** No heading from the filename-owned D1–D40 review/companion corpus is missing from the three part registers. No dropped product requirement was demonstrated by this structural review. The audit did find missing _direct locator entries_ for shared authority/reference material; those now have explicit dispositions and targets rather than being silently omitted.

## Scope and evidence limit

Compared every headed section and file hash in `phase26-spec-coverage-inventory.json` with the actual three final traceability schemas. Checked empty normative targets, duplicate mappings, non-heading evidence rows and unmatched files. Independently inspected the native-CRM precedence, the shared P17/P6 boundary, final ratification/old-question treatment and eight specific final-review correction crosswalks. This is a whole-inventory structural audit with targeted semantic checks, **not** a fresh sentence-by-sentence semantic re-review of all 16.8MB of source capture, a runtime test or proof that all published prose is free of every possible error.

## Exact counts

<!-- prettier-ignore -->

|---|---:|
| Captured files | 591 |

| Actual captured headed sections | 5,815 |

The 5,709 rows already include 105 JSON-evidence rows; do not add those 105 again or describe 5,709 as unique covered headings. Repeated mappings are legitimate because one source section can supply several independently addressable clauses. Non-heading evidence is measured as files/rows, not fabricated Markdown sections.

## Missing direct locators and their exact treatment

- **76 feature-ADR sections (D14–D26):** concise decision, authority, ratification and complete-record summaries alias the final D14–D26 requirement sets. Their root review/contract counterparts were already mapped; the missing locator entries did not justify inventing new behavior or treating the ADRs as ignored.
- **40 Support glossary sections:** canonical terminology maps to the applicable decision requirements and G02/G04/G05/G08. Public/internal guidance retains D27-C; later note/draft/reading/unwanted terminology does not revive older provisional choices.
- **190 ledger/handoff sections:** chronology and ratification indexes retain exact accepted decision targets. Historical questions, proposed-status notices and no-formalization text are evidence; they do not reopen D1–D40 after the user's explicit `/to-spec` and confirmed testing approach.
- **481 platform/reference sections:** the supplemental map distinguishes inherited governing requirements, platform glossary/context, procedural instructions, native-CRM authority, P17/P6 owner and proof contracts, scoped exclusions, predecessor readiness evidence and unrelated roadmap/Phase21 features. Consuming an owner contract does not import that owner's whole feature catalog into Support Hub.
- **12 file-only gaps:** nine historical ratification JSON readbacks and three inspected TypeScript source files now have explicit evidence dispositions. Current code describes implementation reality/gaps; it is neither normative product authority nor a runtime acceptance pass.

The machine supplement uses `sourceFile`, `sourceSection`, `sourceHash`, `sourceRange`, `sourceSectionHash`, `disposition`, `reason` and `targets`. ## Specific authority and correction checks

1. **Native CRM wins.** Governing ADR0001 controls stale vendor-backing/isolated-datastore/synchronization premises in `crm-core`. Valid native owner authorization, identity, recovery and surface rules remain required through G01/G02/G08/G14. The supplement does not declare every CRM requirement obsolete.
2. **P17/P6 remain inherited owners.** Source/compiler/publication, immutable provider material, recipient-specific communication, in-product state, replay, privacy and proof obligations stay at their owners. Other system-message catalogs and Phase21 expense/field-account amendments are not silently promoted into Phase26 capabilities.
3. **D32 final corrections are present.** Stable input key versus fresh technical rendition generation, atomic tentative-to-Ready custody, honest saved formula values and visible saved pivot-result cells map to final R07/R12/R17 and their exact named P cases. Historical final-review classification does not mean those corrections were rejected.
4. **D34 backup correction is present.** Final R20/P29/P34 distinguish prohibited raw topic/draft content in operational diagnostics from protected minimal technical state in actual backup custody. Restore cannot revive an old composing lease; the short row-cleanup target is not a backup-erasure promise.
5. **D39-R25 governance is retained globally.** Its native-CRM winner, exact artifact trace, source preservation and no-probe-as-runtime-proof requirements remain in G01/G08/G14. Only obsolete pending/no-formalization directions are superseded.
6. **Two D1 evidence headings need precise reading.** DB8's intake/attachment “status” and C9's delivery/case “status” describe source findings, not interview-stage status. Their adopted custody, communication and durable-effect requirements already exist in D1/G05–G07/G11. The supplemental correction crosswalk records that distinction explicitly.
